correctness.rationale: Direct partial composition forces domain A∩(A−k) and displacement 2k. Nonempty targets split over the solutions of 2k=j and over their +k cycles; for the empty target the empty input is counted only once. A positive output edge forces both input endpoints to one, so a single zero between positive edges is impossible. For a zero run r=2 there is one forced interior zero; for r≥3 the two end-adjacent input vertices are forced zero and the r−3 free vertices form an independent-set path, giving F_(r−1). The all-one and independent-set-cycle all-zero branches include periods 1 and 2. The trace of the displayed two-bit transition matrix enumerates indexed (not rotation-quotiented) periodic words; its nonzero characteristic factor yields the recurrence. Odd n gives unique root displacement and φ(d) shifts of order d, hence the stated divisor sum with a single empty output. The disjoint-triple bound uses floor(d/3)/d≥1/5 for d≥3 and bounds the entire nonidentity displacement contribution exponentially relative to the monoid. The initial displayed counts also follow from the recurrence. A fresh direct tuple-composition enumeration checked all target fibers for n=1–8 and all local fibers through length 12; the direct image at n=9 was 1702. Direct images at n=1–9 were 2, 4, 16, 25, 96, 136, 428, 597, 1702. Replay the bounded check by enumerating tuples with defined entries x+k modulo n and undefined entries elsewhere, composing each distinct tuple with itself, and tallying outputs including the single empty tuple; enumerate binary words independently for the local check. The frozen checker was inspected, not run.
residual_risks: The separate reproduction is finite; the proof, not the enumeration, establishes all n. The image divisor sum is only for odd n.
